subject: Physiology
chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturition Reflex
stem: Principal site of acidification of urine______.

explanation.text: Principal site of acidification of urine is collecting duct. Acidification occurs in both distal tubule and collecting duct, but collecting duct is more important. The urinary pH of 4.5 (limiting pH) is normally achieved in the collecting ducts. In the late distal tubules and collecting ducts, the tubular epithelium secretes H+ by primary active transport. Primary active secretion of H+ occurs in type A intercalated cells of the late distal tubule and in the collecting tubules. H+ concentration can be increased as much as 900-fold in the collecting tubules.

subject: Physiology
chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturition Reflex
stem: Most important extracellular buffer_____.

explanation.text: The most important extracellular buffer is bicarbonate. The source of bicarbonate is plasma by filtration. It is a noninducible buffer. Proteins are the most abundant intracellular buffer. Phosphate is a minor buffer; the source is plasma by filtration and it is noninducible. Ammonia is a minor buffer, locally produced by tubular cells. Its production increases in metabolic acidosis. It is the only inducible buffer.

subject: Physiology
chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturition Reflex
stem: Normal anion gap is mostly due to_____.

explanation.text: Normal anion gap is mostly due to unmeasured proteins. Normally in plasma, concentrations of anions and cations are equal to maintain electrical neutrality, so no real “anion gap” exists; it is a diagnostic concept. Routinely measured ions are Na+, Cl- and HCO3-. The anion gap is the difference between unmeasured anions and unmeasured cations. Plasma anion gap = [Na+] - [Cl-] - [HCO3-]. The unmeasured cations include calcium, magnesium and potassium. The unmeasured anions include albumin, phosphate, sulphate and organic anions. This is primarily used in measurement of different causes of metabolic acidosis.

subject: Physiology
chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturition Reflex
stem: Normal anion gap is _________ mEq/L.

explanation.text: The normal anion gap ranges between 8 and 16 mEq/L. Only certain cations and anions are routinely measured. The cation normally measured is Na+, and the anions are usually Cl- and HCO3-. Plasma anion gap = [Na+] - [HCO3-] - [Cl-]. The anion gap will increase if unmeasured anions rise or if unmeasured cations fall. The most important unmeasured cations include calcium, magnesium and potassium and the major unmeasured anions are albumin, phosphate, sulfate and other organic anions. Usually the unmeasured anions exceed the unmeasured cations and the anion gap ranges between 8 and 16 mEq/L.

stem: Endocrine functions associated with kidney include all of the following except______.

explanation.text: ANP is secreted by the heart. Endocrine/paracrine functions of the kidney: Renin—granular or juxtaglomerular cells (JG cells) of the juxtaglomerular apparatus (JGA); Erythropoietin—interstitial cells in the peritubular capillary bed; Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2)—renal medullary interstitial cells (RMICs), macula densa, and cells of collecting duct; PGI2 and other prostaglandins—arterioles and glomeruli; 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol (calcitriol or vitamin D3)—cells of proximal tubules of the kidneys.

stem: The major prostanoid synthesized in kidney is ________.

explanation.text: PGE2 is the major prostanoid synthesized in the kidney. It is secreted by RMICs (Renal Medullary Interstitial Cells), macula densa, and cells in the collecting ducts. Prostacyclin (PGI2) and other prostaglandins are secreted by the arterioles and glomeruli. Renal medullary interstitial cells (RMICs) are specialized fibroblast-like cells which are a major site of cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2) and prostaglandin synthase (PGES) expression.

stem: All of the following results in increased renin secretion except _____.

options.label: b
options.text: Increased amount of Na+ in DCT

options.label: c
options.text: Decreased amount of Na+ in PCT

explanation.text: The increased amount of Na+ and Cl- reabsorption across macula densa (DCT) is inhibitory to renin secretion. All other factors increase renin secretion. Renin leads to events through the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone pathway that finally lead to salt and water retention and increased blood pressure. Thus factors that cause decreased effective volume, pressure, or sodium delivery increase renin levels and vice versa. Note: Renin is secreted by juxtaglomerular cells (granular cells), epitheloid cells located in the media of afferent arterioles of the glomerulus.

stem: Vasopressin secretion is increased by_____.

explanation.text: Vasopressin (ADH) secretion increases in response to decreased ECF volume to bring about water retention to restore the ECF volume. ADH exerts its antidiuretic effect by acting on V2 receptors and involves insertion of aquaporin 2 (AQP2) into the apical (luminal) membranes of principal cells of the collecting ducts.

stem: A patient who got into an accident is brought to the casualty and is bleeding from his right leg. His blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. Which of the following plays the most important role for sodium and water retention in this patient?

explanation.text: The renin-angiotensin system plays the most important role for sodium and water retention in this patient as the patient has hypovolemia due to blood loss. The plasma concentration of renin is the rate-limiting step in the renin-angiotensin system; it is the major determinant of plasma angiotensin II concentration. Angiotensin II stimulates aldosterone and ADH secretion; it also constricts blood vessels and causes thirst, which helps in maintaining blood pressure.

stem: Atriopeptin (ANP) acts at _____.

explanation.text: ANP acts on the collecting duct. ANP is secreted by the atria in response to an increase in ECF volume. It decreases Na+ reabsorption in the late distal tubule and collecting ducts and causes natriuresis. ANP causes dilation of afferent arterioles and constriction of efferent arterioles, resulting in increased RBF and increased GFR.

stem: ANP secretion is raised by all except____.

explanation.text: It is increase in ECF volume and not hypovolemia that causes increased secretion of ANP. Stimuli that increase ANP secretion: increased atrial stretch or ventricular stretch, isotonic saline administration, and increased ECF volume. Stimuli that decrease ANP secretion: rising from supine to standing position (as this decreases the central venous pressure).

stem: Several hormones regulate the tubular reabsorption of water and electrolytes at different sites in the nephron physiologically in a patient. Which of the following combination is correct?

explanation.text: The combination which is correct is aldosterone in collecting ducts. Aldosterone acts on principal cells and intercalated cells present in collecting ducts. It regulates ECF volume and Na+ content. Major stimulus for aldosterone secretion is hyperkalemia. Functions include Na+ and H2O reabsorption, K+ and H+ excretion. Angiotensin II acts on efferent arteriole causing vasoconstriction, increases filtration fraction and preserves GFR when RBF falls. ADH acts on principal cells in collecting ducts and stimulates water reabsorption via Aquaporin-2. ANP is released from atria and BNP from ventricles in response to increased volume; it inhibits RAAS, relaxes mesangial cells and promotes natriuresis.

stem: The areas associated with micturition reflex is/are ______________.

explanation.text: The micturition center is located in the pons. The paracentral lobule is also associated with micturition. The micturition reflex is an autonomic spinal cord reflex, but it can be inhibited or facilitated by centers in the brain. These include strong facilitative and inhibitory centers in the brain stem, located mainly in the pons, and centers in the cerebral cortex that are mainly inhibitory but can become excitatory.

subject: Physiology

stem: Ureteric peristalsis is mainly due to____.

options.label: d
options.text: Pacemaker activity of smooth muscles of renal pelvis

explanation.text: Urine flowing from the collecting ducts into the renal calyces stretches the calyces and increases their inherent pacemaker activity, which initiates peristaltic contractions occurring 1 to 5 times per minute that spread to the renal pelvis and then downward along the ureter, forcing urine toward the bladder. The ureters contain smooth muscle and are innervated by sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves and an intramural plexus. Peristaltic contractions are enhanced by parasympathetic stimulation and inhibited by sympathetic stimulation.

subject: Physiology
chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturition Reflex
stem: In micturition reflex, the first change to occur is____.

explanation.text: One of the initial events is relaxation of the muscles of the pelvic floor, and this may cause sufficient downward tug on the detrusor muscle to initiate its contraction. Micturition is fundamentally a spinal reflex facilitated and inhibited by higher brain centers and subject to voluntary control. Stretch receptors in the bladder wall, especially posterior urethra, send signals through pelvic nerves to sacral cord and reflexively back via parasympathetic fibers. As filling continues, reflexes become more frequent and powerful. Once powerful enough, another reflex via pudendal nerves inhibits the external sphincter; urination occurs if this inhibition overcomes voluntary constrictor signals.

subject: Physiology
chapter: Acid-Base Balance, Renal Hormones and Micturition Reflex
stem: How much urine in the bladder will cause the first urge to void in a patient?

explanation.text: The first urge to void is felt at a bladder volume of about 150 mL, and a marked sense of fullness at about 400 mL. A cystometrogram plots intravesical pressure against bladder fluid volume. The curve shows an initial slight rise in pressure with first increments (Ia), a long nearly flat segment with further increments (Ib), and a sudden sharp rise as the micturition reflex is triggered (II). The flatness of segment Ib reflects the law of Laplace: pressure in a spherical viscus equals twice wall tension divided by radius, P = 2T/R. As the bladder fills, tension and radius both increase, so pressure rises only slightly until relatively full.

stem: A patient with salicylic acid poisoning has the following arterial blood gas analysis report: pH = 7.1, pCO2 = 18 mmHg, HCO3- = 12 mmol/L. Identify the acid-base disorder here.

options.label: b
options.text: Respiratory acidosis with compensatory metabolic alkalosis

options.label: c
options.text: Metabolic acidosis with uncompensated respiratory alkalosis

explanation.text: The acid-base disorder is a mixed disorder of metabolic acidosis and respiratory alkalosis. Step 1: pH 7.1 (<7.35) indicates acidosis. Step 2: HCO3- is 12 mmol/L (normal 22-30), indicating metabolic acidosis. Step 3: Winter’s formula: expected pCO2 = (1.5 × [HCO3-]) + 8 ± 2 = 26 ± 2 = 24-28 mmHg. Actual pCO2 is 18 mmHg, indicating overcompensation due to an additional respiratory alkalosis.
